title: Imbalanced Data Handling
description: Imbalanced data handling: Sınıf dağılımı dengesiz (minority %1-10) veri setlerinde çalışma. SMOTE, class weights, focal loss, ensemble methods. Fraud detection, medical diagnosis, anomaly detection.

content.level0_basic: Imbalanced Data, sınıflardan birinin çok az örneği olduğu (minority class) dataset'lerdir. Örnek: Fraud detection (fraud %0.1, normal %99.9), medical diagnosis (kanser %2, sağlıklı %98), spam detection (spam %10, ham %90). Problem: Model majority class'a bias olur (her zaman 'normal' predict → %99.9 accuracy ama hiç fraud yakalamaz!). Accuracy misleading. Metrikler: Precision, Recall, F1-score, ROC-AUC.
content.level1_beginner: Imbalanced data çözümleri: (1) **Resampling**: (a) Oversampling: Minority class'ı duplicate et veya synthetic örnekler oluştur (SMOTE). (b) Undersampling: Majority class'tan random örnekler sil. (2) **Class Weights**: Loss function'da minority class'a daha fazla ağırlık ver (cost-sensitive learning). (3) **Algoritma Seçimi**: Tree-based (Random Forest, XGBoost) imbalanced data'da iyi. (4) **Ensemble**: Majority'yi böl, her parça ile minority'yi train et (EasyEnsemble). (5) **Threshold Tuning**: Probability threshold'ı ayarla (0.5 yerine 0.3). (6) **Metrikler**: Precision (false positive), Recall (false negative), F1 (harmonic mean), ROC-AUC, PR-AUC.
content.level2_application: Pratik uygulamalar: (1) **Fraud Detection**: %0.1-1 fraud. SMOTE + XGBoost + class weights. Cost-sensitive: False negative çok costly. (2) **Medical Diagnosis**: Rare disease (%1-5). High recall kritik (false negative = hasta kaçar). SMOTE + ensemble. (3) **Spam Detection**: %10-30 spam. Threshold tuning (precision vs recall). Undersampling + oversampling hybrid. (4) **Churn Prediction**: %5-10 churn. SMOTE + Random Forest. Feature engineering (customer behavior). (5) **Anomaly Detection**: %0.1-5 anomaly. One-Class SVM, Isolation Forest (unsupervised). (6) **Click Prediction**: CTR %1-5. Focal loss (deep learning), class weights. Framework'ler: imbalanced-learn (SMOTE), XGBoost (scale_pos_weight), TensorFlow (class_weight).
content.level3_advanced: İleri seviye: (1) **SMOTE Variants**: BorderlineSMOTE (borderline örnekler), ADASYN (adaptive synthetic), SVMSMOTE (SVM boundary). (2) **Deep Learning**: Focal Loss (hard examples'a focus), class weights, oversampling minority. Data augmentation (image, text). (3) **Ensemble**: EasyEnsemble (majority'yi böl), BalancedBagging (bootstrap with resampling), RUSBoost (undersampling + boosting). (4) **Cost Matrix**: Asymmetric cost (FN cost >> FP cost). Custom loss function. (5) **Threshold Optimization**: ROC curve → optimal threshold (Youden's J statistic). Precision-Recall curve (F1 max). (6) **Hybrid**: SMOTE + ENN (Edited Nearest Neighbors) → noise removal. SMOTE + Tomek Links → borderline cleanup. (7) **Anomaly-as-Imbalanced**: One-Class SVM, Isolation Forest, Autoencoder (unsupervised approach).
content.level4_expert: Expert seviyede, production trade-offs, domain-specific strategies ve research frontiers önemlidir. (1) **Production**: Model monitoring (minority class metrics), threshold tuning (business KPIs), A/B testing (precision vs recall), retraining strategy (new minority samples). (2) **Domain-Specific**: (a) Finance: Regulatory (false negative costly), explainability (SHAP), fairness (protected attributes). (b) Healthcare: High recall (patient safety), calibration (probability accuracy), ensemble (reduce variance). (c) Fraud: Real-time (streaming), concept drift (fraud patterns change), feedback loop (manual review → retrain). (3) **Multi-class Imbalanced**: One-vs-rest SMOTE, class weight per class, macro/micro F1. (4) **Few-shot Learning**: Siamese networks, prototypical networks, meta-learning (when minority << 100). (5) **Fairness**: Imbalanced + bias (minority class in protected group). Fair oversampling, bias mitigation. (6) **Active Learning**: Label minority samples selectively (uncertainty sampling), reduce labeling cost. (7) **Contrastive Learning**: Self-supervised pre-training, few minority samples fine-tuning. Research: **Zero-shot imbalanced** (no minority training data), **Causal imbalanced** (confounding), **Dynamic imbalanced** (streaming data, concept drift).

whatIsIt: Imbalanced Data: Sınıf dağılımı dengesiz dataset. Matematiksel: Imbalance Ratio (IR) = |majority| / |minority|. IR>10 → imbalanced, IR>100 → extreme. Problem: Model majority bias (accuracy %99 ama minority recall %0). Metrikler: Precision = TP/(TP+FP), Recall = TP/(TP+FN), F1 = 2·(P·R)/(P+R), ROC-AUC (threshold-independent), PR-AUC (imbalanced için better). Çözümler: Resampling (SMOTE, undersampling), Class Weights (cost-sensitive), Threshold Tuning, Ensemble (BalancedBagging), Focal Loss (deep learning).
whyNeeded: Imbalanced data handling kritik çünkü: (1) **Real-world Reality**: Çoğu domain imbalanced (fraud %0.1, cancer %2, spam %10, click %1). Balanced data nadir. (2) **Accuracy Misleading**: Model her zaman 'normal' predict → %99 accuracy ama hiç fraud/cancer yakalamaz! Recall %0. (3) **Cost Asymmetry**: False negative >> false positive cost. Fraud miss ($10K), cancer miss (hayat), spam miss (annoyance). (4) **Minority Critical**: Minority class genellikle critical (fraud, disease, failure). Majority class'a focus yanlış. (5) **Default Algorithms Fail**: Standard ML algorithms majority bias, minority ignore. Naive Bayes, Logistic Regression struggle. (6) **Threshold 0.5 Sub-optimal**: Default threshold imbalanced data'da kötü. Optimal threshold < 0.5 (minority favor). (7) **Evaluation Metrics**: Accuracy değil, Precision/Recall/F1/AUC kullan. Business KPI'lara align et.
realWorldAnalogy: Imbalanced data'yı nadir hastalık teşhisine benzetebiliriz. **Durum**: 10,000 hasta, 50 kanser (%0.5), 9,950 sağlıklı (%99.5). **Naive model**: Her hastaya 'sağlıklı' de → %99.5 accuracy! Ama hiçbir kanser yakalanmadı (recall %0), felaketyön. **Çözümler**: (1) **Oversampling (SMOTE)**: Kanser hastalarını 'sentetik olarak çoğalt' (benzer profillere bakarak). Training: 5,000 kanser, 5,000 sağlıklı → balanced. (2) **Class Weights**: Model'e söyle: 'Kanser miss etme 200x worse'. Loss function'da kanser hatasına 200x ağırlık. (3) **Threshold**: Probability > 0.05 (not 0.5) → 'kanser' de. Daha sensitive, false positive artar ama false negative azalır. **Trade-off**: False positive (sağlıklı hasta gereksiz test) vs False negative (kanser kaçar, ölümcül). Healthcare: False negative >> false positive → high recall prioritize.

formulas: \text{F1-Score}: \quad F_1 = 2 \cdot \frac{P \cdot R}{P + R} = \frac{2 \cdot TP}{2 \cdot TP + FP + FN}
\text{Weighted Loss}: \quad \mathcal{L} = -\frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N w_i \cdot \log p(y_i | x_i) \quad \text{where } w_{\text{minority}} >> w_{\text{majority}}

stepByStep: 1. **Problem Analysis**: Imbalance ratio hesapla (IR = majority/minority). IR>10 → handle gerekir. Minority class kaç örnek? (<100 → extreme). Domain cost: FN vs FP cost nedir?
2. **Baseline**: İlk önce baseline model train et (no handling). Metrikler: Accuracy (misleading), Precision, Recall, F1, ROC-AUC, PR-AUC. Confusion matrix: TP, TN, FP, FN.

3. **Metric Selection**: Business KPI'ya göre: (a) High Recall (healthcare, fraud) → false negative costly. (b) High Precision (spam, marketing) → false positive costly. (c) Balanced: F1-score. (d) Threshold-free: ROC-AUC, PR-AUC.

4. **Strategy Selection**: (a) IR<50: Class weights + threshold tuning. (b) IR<100: SMOTE + class weights. (c) IR>100: SMOTE + ensemble (EasyEnsemble, BalancedBagging). (d) Deep learning: Focal loss + data augmentation. (e) Extreme (<100 minority): Few-shot learning, anomaly detection.

5. **Resampling**: (a) Oversampling: SMOTE (synthetic), Random oversampling (duplicate). (b) Undersampling: Random (majority'den sil), Tomek Links (borderline). (c) Hybrid: SMOTE+ENN, SMOTE+Tomek. Split BEFORE resampling (test clean).

6. **Model Training**: (a) Class weights: sklearn class_weight='balanced', XGBoost scale_pos_weight=IR. (b) Loss function: Focal loss (PyTorch), weighted cross-entropy. (c) Algorithm: Tree-based (RF, XGBoost), ensemble (Bagging), deep learning (with focal loss).

7. **Threshold Tuning**: Default 0.5 sub-optimal. (a) ROC curve → Youden's J statistic (max sensitivity + specificity). (b) PR curve → max F1. (c) Business KPI → custom threshold (örn: Recall≥0.9). (d) Validation: Separate validation set.

8. **Evaluation**: Test set (imbalanced, original distribution). Metrikler: Precision, Recall, F1, ROC-AUC, PR-AUC. Confusion matrix analizi: FP rate, FN rate. Stratified CV (her fold'da minority represent).
9. **Error Analysis**: FN analizi (hangi minority miss?), FP analizi (hangi majority false alarm?). Feature importance (SHAP): Hangi features discriminative? Borderline examples: Hard cases nerede?

10. **Production Deployment**: Monitor minority class metrics (Recall, F1). Threshold adaptation (business KPI change). Retraining: New minority samples → retrain. A/B testing: New strategy vs old. Fairness check (protected attributes).
algorithm.complexity: **Zaman Karmaşıklığı**: SMOTE: O(N·k·D) (k=neighbors), Random oversampling: O(N), Undersampling: O(N), Class weights: No overhead (same as base model), Focal loss: O(N·C) per batch. **Training**: Resampling once O(N), then model training (depends on model). **Uzay**: SMOTE: O(synthetic_samples·D), Oversampling: 2-10x original data. **Inference**: No overhead (resampling only at training). **Scalability**: SMOTE scalable (k-NN with KDTree O(log N)), Undersampling reduces data. Big data: Spark MLlib (random resampling), Dask.

codeExamples.title: Baseline: Imbalanced Data Problem
codeExamples.code:
import numpy as np
from sklearn.datasets import make_classification
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, confusion_matrix, roc_auc_score
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Imbalanced dataset: 95% class 0, 5% class 1
X, y = make_classification(
    n_samples=10000,
    n_features=20,
    n_informative=15,
    n_redundant=5,
    weights=[0.95, 0.05],  # Imbalance ratio = 19:1
    flip_y=0.01,
    random_state=42
)

print(f'Total: {len(y)}')
print(f'Class 0: {(y==0).sum()} ({(y==0).mean()*100:.1f}%)')
print(f'Class 1: {(y==1).sum()} ({(y==1).mean()*100:.1f}%)')
print(f'Imbalance Ratio: {(y==0).sum()/(y==1).sum():.1f}:1')

X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.3, random_state=42, stratify=y)

# Naive model (no handling)
clf = LogisticRegression(random_state=42, max_iter=1000)
clf.fit(X_train, y_train)
y_pred = clf.predict(X_test)

print('\n=== NAIVE MODEL (No Imbalance Handling) ===')
print(f'Accuracy: {(y_pred == y_test).mean():.3f}')  # Misleading!
print('\nClassification Report:')
print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred, target_names=['Class 0', 'Class 1']))

print('\nConfusion Matrix:')
print(confusion_matrix(y_test, y_pred))
print('Note: High accuracy but poor recall for Class 1 (minority)!')

print(f'\nROC-AUC: {roc_auc_score(y_test, clf.predict_proba(X_test)[:, 1]):.3f}')
codeExamples.explanation: Baseline: Imbalanced data (95%/5%). Naive model → high accuracy (%95) ama minority recall poor. Accuracy misleading!

codeExamples.title: SMOTE (Synthetic Minority Oversampling)
codeExamples.code:
import numpy as np
from sklearn.datasets import make_classification
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, confusion_matrix, roc_auc_score
from imblearn.over_sampling import SMOTE
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Imbalanced data
X, y = make_classification(
    n_samples=10000,
    n_features=20,
    n_informative=15,
    weights=[0.95, 0.05],
    random_state=42
)

X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.3, random_state=42, stratify=y)

print('Before SMOTE:')
print(f'Train - Class 0: {(y_train==0).sum()}, Class 1: {(y_train==1).sum()}')

# SMOTE: Synthetic minority oversampling
smote = SMOTE(random_state=42, k_neighbors=5)
X_train_smote, y_train_smote = smote.fit_resample(X_train, y_train)

print('\nAfter SMOTE:')
print(f'Train - Class 0: {(y_train_smote==0).sum()}, Class 1: {(y_train_smote==1).sum()}')
print(f'Now balanced!')

# Train with SMOTE
clf = LogisticRegression(random_state=42, max_iter=1000)
clf.fit(X_train_smote, y_train_smote)
y_pred = clf.predict(X_test)

print('\n=== MODEL WITH SMOTE ===')
print(f'Accuracy: {(y_pred == y_test).mean():.3f}')
print('\nClassification Report:')
print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred, target_names=['Class 0', 'Class 1']))

print('\nConfusion Matrix:')
print(confusion_matrix(y_test, y_pred))

print(f'\nROC-AUC: {roc_auc_score(y_test, clf.predict_proba(X_test)[:, 1]):.3f}')
print('Note: Better recall for minority class!')
codeExamples.explanation: SMOTE: Synthetic minority samples (k-NN based). Balance training data. Minority recall ↑, overall performance better.

codeExamples.title: Class Weights (Cost-Sensitive)
codeExamples.code:
import numpy as np
from sklearn.datasets import make_classification
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, confusion_matrix, roc_auc_score
from sklearn.utils.class_weight import compute_class_weight

# Imbalanced data
X, y = make_classification(
    n_samples=10000,
    n_features=20,
    n_informative=15,
    weights=[0.95, 0.05],
    random_state=42
)

X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.3, random_state=42, stratify=y)

# Compute class weights
classes = np.unique(y_train)
weights = compute_class_weight('balanced', classes=classes, y=y_train)
class_weight_dict = {classes[i]: weights[i] for i in range(len(classes))}

print('Class weights (balanced):')
print(class_weight_dict)
print(f'Minority class weight is {weights[1]/weights[0]:.1f}x higher')

# Model WITHOUT class weights
clf_no_weight = LogisticRegression(random_state=42, max_iter=1000)
clf_no_weight.fit(X_train, y_train)
y_pred_no_weight = clf_no_weight.predict(X_test)

print('\n=== WITHOUT Class Weights ===')
print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred_no_weight, target_names=['Class 0', 'Class 1']))

# Model WITH class weights
clf_weight = LogisticRegression(class_weight='balanced', random_state=42, max_iter=1000)
clf_weight.fit(X_train, y_train)
y_pred_weight = clf_weight.predict(X_test)

print('\n=== WITH Class Weights ===')
print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred_weight, target_names=['Class 0', 'Class 1']))

print('\nComparison:')
print(f'Without weights - ROC-AUC: {roc_auc_score(y_test, clf_no_weight.predict_proba(X_test)[:, 1]):.3f}')
print(f'With weights    - ROC-AUC: {roc_auc_score(y_test, clf_weight.predict_proba(X_test)[:, 1]):.3f}')
print('Note: Class weights improve minority recall!')
codeExamples.explanation: Class Weights: Minority class'a daha fazla ağırlık. Loss function'da minority error >> majority error. Basit, etkili.

codeExamples.title: Threshold Tuning
codeExamples.code:
import numpy as np
from sklearn.datasets import make_classification
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.metrics import precision_recall_curve, roc_curve, f1_score
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Imbalanced data
X, y = make_classification(
    n_samples=10000,
    n_features=20,
    n_informative=15,
    weights=[0.95, 0.05],
    random_state=42
)

X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.3, random_state=42, stratify=y)

# Train
clf = LogisticRegression(class_weight='balanced', random_state=42, max_iter=1000)
clf.fit(X_train, y_train)

# Probabilities
y_proba = clf.predict_proba(X_test)[:, 1]

# Find optimal threshold (max F1)
precisions, recalls, thresholds_pr = precision_recall_curve(y_test, y_proba)
f1_scores = 2 * (precisions * recalls) / (precisions + recalls + 1e-10)
optimal_idx = np.argmax(f1_scores)
optimal_threshold = thresholds_pr[optimal_idx] if optimal_idx < len(thresholds_pr) else 0.5

print(f'Default threshold: 0.5')
print(f'Optimal threshold (max F1): {optimal_threshold:.3f}')

# Predictions with different thresholds
y_pred_default = (y_proba >= 0.5).astype(int)
y_pred_optimal = (y_proba >= optimal_threshold).astype(int)

print('\n=== Default Threshold (0.5) ===')
print(f'F1-score: {f1_score(y_test, y_pred_default):.3f}')

print('\n=== Optimal Threshold ({:.3f}) ==='.format(optimal_threshold))
print(f'F1-score: {f1_score(y_test, y_pred_optimal):.3f}')

# Visualization
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 4))

# Precision-Recall curve
axes[0].plot(recalls, precisions, label='PR Curve')
axes[0].scatter(recalls[optimal_idx], precisions[optimal_idx], c='red', s=100, marker='x', label=f'Optimal (th={optimal_threshold:.2f})')
axes[0].set_xlabel('Recall')
axes[0].set_ylabel('Precision')
axes[0].set_title('Precision-Recall Curve')
axes[0].legend()
axes[0].grid(alpha=0.3)

# F1 vs Threshold
axes[1].plot(thresholds_pr, f1_scores[:-1], label='F1-score')
axes[1].axvline(optimal_threshold, color='r', linestyle='--', label=f'Optimal={optimal_threshold:.2f}')
axes[1].set_xlabel('Threshold')
axes[1].set_ylabel('F1-Score')
axes[1].set_title('F1-Score vs Threshold')
axes[1].legend()
axes[1].grid(alpha=0.3)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

print('\nNote: Optimal threshold < 0.5 for imbalanced data!')
codeExamples.explanation: Threshold Tuning: Default 0.5 sub-optimal. Precision-Recall curve → max F1 threshold. Imbalanced: optimal < 0.5.

codeExamples.title: Ensemble: BalancedBagging
codeExamples.code:
import numpy as np
from sklearn.datasets import make_classification
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, roc_auc_score
from imblearn.ensemble import BalancedBaggingClassifier
from sklearn.tree import DecisionTreeClassifier

# Imbalanced data
X, y = make_classification(
    n_samples=10000,
    n_features=20,
    n_informative=15,
    weights=[0.95, 0.05],
    random_state=42
)

X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.3, random_state=42, stratify=y)

print('Training data:')
print(f'Class 0: {(y_train==0).sum()}, Class 1: {(y_train==1).sum()}')

# BalancedBaggingClassifier
# Each bootstrap sample is balanced (undersample majority)
bbc = BalancedBaggingClassifier(
    estimator=DecisionTreeClassifier(max_depth=5, random_state=42),
    n_estimators=10,
    random_state=42,
    n_jobs=-1
)

print('\nTraining BalancedBagging...')
bbc.fit(X_train, y_train)
y_pred = bbc.predict(X_test)

print('\n=== BalancedBagging Results ===')
print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred, target_names=['Class 0', 'Class 1']))

print(f'\nROC-AUC: {roc_auc_score(y_test, bbc.predict_proba(X_test)[:, 1]):.3f}')

print('\nHow it works:')
print('1. Create N bootstrap samples')
print('2. Each sample: undersample majority to match minority')
print('3. Train weak learner on each balanced sample')
print('4. Ensemble: vote/average predictions')
print('Benefit: Diversity + balance → better minority recall')
codeExamples.explanation: BalancedBagging: Ensemble, her bootstrap balanced (majority undersample). Diversity + balance → minority recall ↑.

codeExamples.title: Focal Loss (Deep Learning)
codeExamples.code:
import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F
from sklearn.datasets import make_classification
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, roc_auc_score

# Focal Loss: Focus on hard examples
class FocalLoss(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, alpha=0.25, gamma=2.0):
        super().__init__()
        self.alpha = alpha
        self.gamma = gamma
    
    def forward(self, inputs, targets):
        BCE_loss = F.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits(inputs, targets, reduction='none')
        pt = torch.exp(-BCE_loss)  # p_t
        focal_loss = self.alpha * (1 - pt) ** self.gamma * BCE_loss
        return focal_loss.mean()

# Data
X, y = make_classification(
    n_samples=10000,
    n_features=20,
    n_informative=15,
    weights=[0.95, 0.05],
    random_state=42
)

X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.3, random_state=42, stratify=y)

X_train_t = torch.FloatTensor(X_train)
y_train_t = torch.FloatTensor(y_train).unsqueeze(1)
X_test_t = torch.FloatTensor(X_test)

print('Training with Focal Loss...')

# Simple NN
model = nn.Sequential(
    nn.Linear(20, 64),
    nn.ReLU(),
    nn.Linear(64, 32),
    nn.ReLU(),
    nn.Linear(32, 1)
)

optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=0.001)
focal_loss = FocalLoss(alpha=0.25, gamma=2.0)

# Train
for epoch in range(50):
    model.train()
    optimizer.zero_grad()
    outputs = model(X_train_t)
    loss = focal_loss(outputs, y_train_t)
    loss.backward()
    optimizer.step()
    
    if (epoch + 1) % 10 == 0:
        print(f'Epoch {epoch+1}, Loss: {loss.item():.4f}')

# Evaluate
model.eval()
with torch.no_grad():
    y_proba = torch.sigmoid(model(X_test_t)).numpy().flatten()
    y_pred = (y_proba >= 0.5).astype(int)

print('\n=== Focal Loss Results ===')
print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred, target_names=['Class 0', 'Class 1']))
print(f'\nROC-AUC: {roc_auc_score(y_test, y_proba):.3f}')

print('\nFocal Loss: FL = -α(1-p_t)^γ log(p_t)')
print('γ=2: Hard examples (low p_t) get higher loss')
print('α=0.25: Weight for minority class')
print('Benefit: Focus on misclassified minority samples')
codeExamples.explanation: Focal Loss: Hard examples'a focus (γ parameter). Deep learning için ideal. Minority class için α weight. Down-weight easy examples.

options: Default 0.5 imbalanced'da sub-optimal. Optimal < 0.5 (minority favor). PR curve → max F1
quiz.explanation: Default threshold 0.5 balanced data için. Imbalanced: optimal < 0.5. PR curve → max F1 threshold. Youden's J statistic (ROC).

quiz.question: Focal Loss'un avantajı nedir?
options: Hard examples'a focus (γ parameter). Easy examples down-weight. Deep learning için
quiz.explanation: Focal Loss: FL = -α(1-p_t)^γ log(p_t). γ=2: hard examples (low p_t) → high loss. α: minority weight. Down-weight easy examples.

quiz.question: Undersampling vs Oversampling?
options: Undersampling: majority'den sil (data loss). Oversampling: minority çoğalt (overfitting risk)
quiz.explanation: Undersampling: Majority'den random sil (data loss, information loss). Oversampling: Minority duplicate/synthetic (overfitting risk, training slow). Hybrid: ikisini combine.

quiz.question: Production'da imbalanced data challenge?
options: Minority metrics monitor, threshold tuning (business KPI), concept drift, retraining strategy
quiz.explanation: Production: (1) Monitor minority Recall/F1, (2) Threshold tune (business KPI), (3) Concept drift (retrain), (4) A/B test, (5) Fairness (protected attributes), (6) Feedback loop.

flashcards.back: Sınıf dağılımı dengesiz. IR = majority/minority. IR>10 imbalanced, IR>100 extreme. Problem: Model majority bias, accuracy misleading.
Synthetic Minority Oversampling. k-NN based: x_new = x + λ(x_nn - x). Balance training data. Variants: BorderlineSMOTE, ADASYN, SVMSMOTE.
Cost-sensitive learning. Loss'ta minority'ye >> weight. sklearn: class_weight='balanced'. XGBoost: scale_pos_weight=IR. Basit, etkili.
Precision = TP/(TP+FP) (FP rate). Recall = TP/(TP+FN) (FN rate). F1 = harmonic mean. Trade-off: High recall → low precision.
Default 0.5 sub-optimal. PR curve → max F1. ROC → Youden's J. Imbalanced: optimal < 0.5 (minority favor).
FL = -α(1-p_t)^γ log(p_t). γ=2: hard examples focus. α: minority weight. Down-weight easy. Deep learning için ideal.
Ensemble: Her bootstrap balanced (undersample majority). Diversity + balance → minority recall ↑. imbalanced-learn.
Majority'den sil (random, Tomek Links). Data loss ama faster training. Extreme imbalance'da (IR>100) useful.
Minority çoğalt. Random (duplicate), SMOTE (synthetic). Overfitting risk ama information preserve.
ROC-AUC: Threshold-free, TPR vs FPR. PR-AUC: Imbalanced için better, Precision vs Recall. PR-AUC < ROC-AUC (imbalanced).
Asymmetric cost: C(FN) >> C(FP). Healthcare: FN = patient death. Fraud: FN = $10K loss. Custom loss function.
Minority metrics (Recall, F1), threshold adaptation, concept drift, retraining, A/B test, fairness check.

commonMistakes.why: Imbalanced'da accuracy misleading. Model her zaman 'normal' → %99 acc ama minority recall %0. Kritik sınıfı kaçırır (fraud, cancer).
commonMistakes.fix: Metrikler: Precision, Recall, F1, ROC-AUC, PR-AUC. Confusion matrix analizi (TP, TN, FP, FN). Business KPI'ya align et (cost of FN vs FP).

commonMistakes.why: Test set original distribution olmalı (production distribution). Test'i resample → overly optimistic results, production'da fail.
commonMistakes.fix: Sadece training set'i resample et. Test/validation original (imbalanced) kalsın. Stratified split (her fold'da minority represent).

commonMistakes.why: SMOTE before split → data leakage (synthetic örnekler test'e gider). Overly optimistic results, production fail.
commonMistakes.fix: Split first (train/test), then SMOTE only on training. Test clean (original distribution). Cross-validation: SMOTE inside each fold.

commonMistakes.why: Default 0.5 balanced data için. Imbalanced: sub-optimal, minority miss. Precision-Recall trade-off'u handle edemez.
commonMistakes.fix: Threshold tuning: PR curve → max F1, ROC → Youden's J. Business KPI (örn: Recall≥0.9). Optimal < 0.5 (minority favor).

commonMistakes.why: Synthetic data + complex model (deep NN) → overfitting minority patterns. Validation good, test bad.
commonMistakes.fix: Regularization (L2, dropout), simpler model (tree-based), cross-validation (monitor val/test gap), early stopping, data augmentation diversity.

commonMistakes.why: Resampling alone yetersiz olabilir (extreme imbalance). Model hala majority bias. SMOTE + training slow (2-10x data).
commonMistakes.fix: Hybrid: SMOTE + class weights (double protection). Or: Undersampling + oversampling + class weights. Ensemble: BalancedBagging, EasyEnsemble.

commonMistakes.why: Imbalanced + protected attributes (race, gender) → bias amplification. Minority class'ta protected group over/under represented. Legal risk.
commonMistakes.fix: Fairness metrics (demographic parity, equal opportunity). Fair oversampling (balance per group). Bias mitigation (reweighting, adversarial debiasing).
